title: A treaty that felt like a loss was called a clear victory.
subtitle: Hudaybiyyah, renamed by Allah

key.label: How it looked and what it was

then: In 6 AH the Prophet ﷺ set out for Umrah and was stopped near Makkah. A treaty sent them home until the next year, and {trap}some Companions, including Umar, disliked its terms.{/trap} On the way back this surah called it {reward}a clear victory.{/reward} Ibn Kathir says the peace let people meet openly, and many embraced Islam.
now: You did not get the job. The move fell through. The deal you wanted had to be signed on worse terms. {trap}It feels like losing.{/trap} {idea}Hudaybiyyah is a reminder that what looks like a step back can be the opening.{/idea}
old: If it does not go the way I planned, it is a loss.
new: What looks like a setback to me can be the victory Allah is preparing.
try: Think of one past disappointment that later turned out well. Thank Allah for it by name.

title: Fully forgiven, and still standing long in prayer.
subtitle: Forgiveness that leads to more gratitude
then: Umar heard the Prophet ﷺ say a surah had come to him {reward}dearer to him than this life and all it holds.{/reward} Ibn Kathir notes this complete forgiveness was a special honor for him alone. Al-Mughirah said he still prayed for very long, and when asked why, {idea}he said: should I not be a thankful servant?{/idea}
now: Someone forgives a debt you owed. You could just feel relieved. Or you could find a way to show thanks for years. {idea}The Prophet ﷺ answered the greatest forgiveness with more worship, out of gratitude.{/idea}
old: Once I am forgiven, I can ease off.
new: Being forgiven is a reason to give thanks with more effort, not less.
try: Add two extra rakahs tonight with the intention of simply saying thank you.

title: Mighty help came through choosing to respect Allah's limits.
subtitle: The she-camel that knelt
then: Ibn Kathir recounts that when his camel refused to move, the Prophet ﷺ said {idea}He who stopped the elephant has stopped her too.{/idea} He said that day he would grant any request that respected Allah's sacred limits. {reward}When he obeyed and accepted peace, Allah promised him mighty help.{/reward}
now: You could win the argument with your sibling by force: louder voice, better facts. {idea}Or you could stop, and choose the path that keeps the peace and honors Allah.{/idea} {reward}That second road is where the help came from at Hudaybiyyah.{/reward}
new: Help can come from stopping and choosing what honors Allah.
try: In one conflict today, choose the response that keeps the peace, even if you could win.

title: Calm sent into hearts so faith could grow.
subtitle: Sakinah at Hudaybiyyah
then: Ibn Kathir says the Companions accepted the call of Allah and His Messenger ﷺ at Hudaybiyyah. {reward}When their hearts settled into acceptance, Allah increased their faith.{/reward} Al-Bukhari used this verse as proof that {idea}faith increases and decreases.{/idea} To Allah belong the armies of the heavens and earth.
now: The surgery date is set, the decision has been made, and you cannot control the rest. {reward}Sometimes calm arrives right when you stop fighting what Allah decided.{/reward} {idea}And faith quietly grows in that calm.{/idea}
old: My faith is what it is; it does not really change.
new: Faith can grow, and calm from Allah is one way He grows it.
try: Ask Allah for sakinah by name in your next prayer.

title: And what about us? The answer was gardens.
subtitle: Good news for the believers too
then: When the Prophet ﷺ recited the verse of his forgiveness, the Companions said congratulations, but what about us? Anas reports this verse was the reply. {reward}Believing men and believing women would enter gardens forever, with their sins wiped away.{/reward} {idea}That, with Allah, is the supreme success.{/idea}
now: You hear about someone else's blessings, a friend's promotion or a cousin's Hajj, and a small voice asks: and me? {reward}Allah answered that question for every believing man and woman.{/reward} There is a share for you too.
old: The great promises are for special people, not ordinary ones like me.
new: Allah's promise of Paradise is for every believing man and woman, including me.
try: When you feel left out of someone's blessing today, ask Allah for Paradise instead.

title: Expecting the worst from Allah is its own downfall.
subtitle: Bad assumptions about Allah
then: Ibn Kathir says the hypocrites and idolaters {trap}questioned the wisdom in Allah's decisions and thought the Prophet ﷺ and his Companions would be killed off.{/trap} The verse says the evil they expected falls on them instead.
now: The test results are delayed and your mind writes the worst story: Allah has given up on me. {trap}That assumption is the real danger.{/trap} {reward}Think well of Allah while you wait.{/reward}
old: When things look bad, Allah must be against me.
new: Assuming the worst about Allah is a trap; His decisions carry wisdom.
try: Next time you catch a worst-case thought today, replace it with one sentence of trust.

title: Every army of heaven and earth already belongs to Him.
subtitle: Repeated for those who doubted His power
then: The same words appeared in verse 4, after the calm sent to believers. {idea}Here they follow the warning to those who thought evil of Allah.{/idea} Ibn Kathir says it asserts {trap}His ability to take revenge on His enemies{/trap}, and that He is Mighty and Wise.
now: You feel outmatched: a bigger company, a louder family member, a system that seems rigged. {idea}Every force you fear already belongs to Allah.{/idea} {reward}For the believer that is comfort; for the one who doubts Him, a warning.{/reward}
old: The powers I fear are bigger than anything protecting me.
new: Every force in heaven and earth belongs to Allah, so I fear Him and trust Him.
try: Name the force you fear most right now and say: this too belongs to Allah.

title: Witness, bringer of good news, and warner.
subtitle: Three roles of the Prophet ﷺ
then: Right after the Hudaybiyyah verses, Allah describes the Prophet ﷺ. Ibn Kathir explains: {idea}a witness over the creation, a bearer of good news to the believers, and a warner to the disbelievers.{/idea}
now: When you share your faith, you might lean only on warnings, or only on comfort. {idea}The Prophet ﷺ carried both.{/idea} {reward}Good news first for those who believe, honest warning for those at risk.{/reward}
old: Talking about faith means either scaring people or only comforting them.
new: The Prophet ﷺ brought both good news and warning, and I can keep both.
try: Share one hopeful verse with someone today, the way he brought good news.

title: Believe, honor the Prophet ﷺ, and glorify Allah morning and evening.
subtitle: Why he was sent, for us

row.title: believe
sub: in Allah and His Messenger ﷺ

then: Ibn Kathir explains the words: honor him, according to Ibn Abbas; {idea}respect and high regard for the Prophet ﷺ{/idea}; and {reward}glorifying Allah in the early and late parts of the day.{/reward}
now: Morning: alarm, phone, news. Evening: commute, dinner, phone again. {idea}The verse asks you to bookend the day with glorifying Allah.{/idea} {reward}Two minutes at each end changes the frame of everything in between.{/reward}
old: Remembering Allah fits in whenever I get a spare moment.
new: I can glorify Allah at both ends of my day, every day.
try: Say subhanAllah 33 times before you check your phone tomorrow morning.

title: The hand of Allah was over their hands.
subtitle: The pledge under the tree
then: Ibn Kathir recounts that Uthman went to Makkah as envoy, and a rumor came that he was killed. The Prophet ﷺ took a pledge from the Companions under a tree; Jabir said {idea}it was a pledge not to run away.{/idea} {reward}Pledging to him was pledging to Allah, and Allah's hand was over theirs.{/reward} The news about Uthman later proved untrue.
now: You make promises all the time: I'll be there, I'll pay you back, I'll call. {idea}A promise made for Allah's sake is made in front of Him.{/idea} {trap}Breaking it hurts you most.{/trap} {reward}Keeping it is worth more than you think.{/reward}
old: Promises are just words; people break them all the time.
new: A promise made for Allah is witnessed by Him, and keeping it brings great reward.
try: Keep one small promise today that you have been putting off.

title: We were busy with family and money, please pray for us.
subtitle: An excuse the tongue says and the heart does not
then: Some bedouins skipped the journey to Hudaybiyyah. Ibn Kathir says they later {trap}claimed they were busy with homes and wealth, and asked for prayers not from faith but to show off.{/trap} {idea}They said with their tongues what was not in their hearts.{/idea} No one could stop what Allah intends.
now: You skip the family visit, the volunteering, the study circle. Then you say: so sorry, work was crazy. {trap}Sometimes true, sometimes not.{/trap} {idea}Allah knows which one it was.{/idea}
old: A polite excuse is harmless as long as people accept it.
new: Allah knows whether my excuse matches my heart, so I can be honest.
try: The next time you decline something today, give your real reason, kindly.

title: You thought they would never come home.
subtitle: The real reason they stayed behind
then: Ibn Kathir explains: {trap}your staying behind was not a simple lapse; it came from thinking the Muslims would all be killed and never return.{/trap} They let that idea settle and feel right. Ibn Abbas and Mujahid said the word bur means headed for destruction.
now: You do not join the new project because, honestly, you expect it to fail and do not want to be on the losing side. {trap}The excuse was being busy. The real reason was low trust.{/trap} {idea}Notice what you are betting on.{/idea}
old: I stayed out because I was busy, nothing more.
new: Sometimes I stay out of good things because I do not trust Allah's promise.
try: Ask yourself honestly why you avoided one good thing recently. Write the real reason.

title: Outward show without inner belief does not hold.
subtitle: Belief in Allah and His Messenger ﷺ, inside and out

row.title: belief inside
sub: in Allah and His Messenger ﷺ

then: After exposing the excuses, the verse states the principle. Ibn Kathir says {trap}whoever does not purify his deeds inwardly and outwardly for Allah will be punished, even if he shows people he follows the faith.{/trap}
now: You can look the part: the right words at the dinner table, the right posts. {idea}The verse asks what is under the surface.{/idea} {reward}A small, sincere faith is worth more than a big performance.{/reward}
old: As long as I look religious, I am fine.
new: Allah wants belief that is real inside, not only a show outside.
try: Do one good deed today that nobody will ever know about.

title: He owns everything, and He is Forgiving and Merciful.
subtitle: The door left open, even after the warnings
then: After the excuses and the warnings to those who stayed behind, the passage ends on Allah's ownership of everything. Ibn Kathir says {reward}He is Forgiving and Merciful to those who repent, return, and humble themselves before Him.{/reward}
now: You read the last few verses and recognized yourself: the excuses, the low trust, the show. {reward}The verse does not end with a slammed door.{/reward} {idea}It ends with Forgiving, Merciful.{/idea}
old: After all my excuses, Allah must have given up on me.
new: Allah owns everything, and His forgiveness is open to anyone who returns.
try: Say one honest sentence to Allah tonight about an excuse you made, and ask forgiveness.

title: Absent for the hard part, eager for the reward.
subtitle: Those who stayed behind asked to come to Khaybar
then: Ibn Kathir says when the Prophet ﷺ later set out for Khaybar, those who had stayed behind {trap}wanted to come for the spoils, having missed the time of hardship.{/trap} {idea}Allah had already promised Khaybar to those at Hudaybiyyah.{/idea} They accused the believers of envy, but understood little.
now: The group project: one person did nothing for weeks, then wants their name on the final slide. {trap}You might do the same in your own way: skip the effort, want the reward.{/trap} {idea}The reward follows the hardship.{/idea}
old: I can show up at the end and still share in the result.
new: The reward belongs to those who stayed through the hard part.
try: Show up for one hard part of something today, not just the easy finish.
